comment: Dr. Ware is clearly caring and approached this course very efficiently. This was one of my favorite courses I have taken at UR so far. It is an excellent start to programming and fulfills a gen ed. I would highly recommend this course with her.

A lot of Ware's classes can be rough, but since Android Programming is a CMSC elective, you should have some background knowledge going in. At that point, this class will actually be really easy and fun! You'll learn a lot about making apps, and the she knows what she's talking about this time! Office hours are also super helpful for this class.
Unless you have previous coding knowledge this class will be a struggle. Her lecture slides are not that helpful. Try to take a different class if you can. She is very nice though.
Avoid Dr.Ware if you can. Terrible at teaching and doesn't even know the material herself.

If you have no previous knowledge of coding or computer science, it may be difficult to understand some of the concepts and terminology. But Dr.Ware is patient and will work with you to help you understand. She does speed through the topics quickly and you have to spend a lot of time outside of class to stay on track.

Prof Ware is good, not much homework and there was no actual lab. But the class itself is boring. She is not very good at making them interesting but this is a mandatory course for a CS major so she is one of the best options for CMSC222

I did not have prior coding knowledge - so I struggled with the material. She teaches well tho. No prior reading, just show up and learn everything at once and that doesn't work too well for me. She gave out amount of weekly hw, quiz(which reflect the lectures), and lab are reasonable. her exam is kinda hard and you just gotta do the work for A

Spends way too little time on the most important material(s). At first thought this was just a 222 thing, but seems to be consistent across classes. I myself tried asking a question once, got a completely unrelated response; never tried going to office hours again. Everyone in my class is bracing for a mediocre grade. Only take as a last resort.

This is her first year teaching this, and it shows. She cares about teaching the content, but struggles with pacing, explaining difficult concepts, and adopting the content into individual work. In the future, I expect she will be great with teaching this subject, but I'd say wait until she gets more comfortable with this course (1-2 years) first.
She is good at making things clear!

Awful teacher. She makes it clear that she's trying to punish and not help you. She gives 2 assignments and a quiz every week and doesn't provide any usefulness when you ask for help. She's smart, but has no idea how to teach and never gives satisfying answers to questions. The material is fairly easy and I participated a lot, yet somehow got a B

Dr. Ware is a nice professor but her lectures are taught at a rapid speed making it very hard to obtain information, especially if you are new to the topic. You will not receive grades until months later which tremendously impacts your weekly quizzes because you are unable to see your mistakes along the way. Labs are long and barely weighted.

The only bad thing about her CMSC 150 is the grader. She won't return the grade until she's told to do so. You'll be doing quizzes making the same mistakes over and over again which could have been fixed if the grader grades them on time and gives you feedback on your work. She will still take points off for those mistakes, though, which sucks.

Dr. Ware is clearly very knowledgeable, but she is completely unable to transfer that knowledge to her students, often leaving them more confused after asking questions. Sometimes she would even start to answer questions you didn't even ask when you tried to get help with something specific. It was easier to learn on your own than listen to her.
